section_entries.label: Proof of Theorem 2
section_entries.mathematical_role: Adapts the barriers to a lower endpoint constraint, converts maxima to contour integrals, proves new derandomization lemmas, and combines them to obtain the FHK-scale upper tail.

unit_result_entry.title: The lower smooth threshold is transferred to a random terminal barrier and closes Key Proposition 4
unit_result_entry.why_material: On G̃_t, the truncated exponential from Lemma 6 is comparable to the Euler-product block product, so a large smooth sum implies a terminal lower product barrier except for a controlled approximation error. The proof then repeats smooth-majorant Taylor derandomization with a shifted j=0 constraint, invokes Lemma 7, and checks degree, leakage, length, and truncation errors.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Conditioning away tiny primes lets the Gaussian ballot theorem control the lower endpoint
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Lemma 7 augments the random good event with a strong lower bound on the full product. It conditions on the contribution of the smallest-prime blocks to restore the hypotheses of an imported Euler-product-to-Gaussian comparison, then applies Probability Result 1 to obtain separate upper-barrier and terminal-window factors.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Cauchy localization turns a point maximum into averaged contour mass; the fourth-moment lemma forces that mass through a large smooth factor, so after derandomization the problem is a Gaussian path staying below an upper barrier and ending in a narrow high window, yielding the 3/4 correction.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: This proves only an upper tail with iterated-log losses; the full FHK distribution and matching lower tail remain conjectural.
